name: Migration lane (batch apply + merge of migration PRs, per project)
cadence: */10 * * * * (via bin/migration-lane.sh, the migration-lane dispatcher: one run per project through bin/lib/project-lanes.sh)

knobs.note: Ready migration PRs one batch may carry (row lane.migration[.<project>].batch_max). The rest ride the next tick.
How long the lane waits for the batch PR's CI before it closes the batch, alerts and applies nothing. Counted as CI_POLL_S per poll.
Seconds between two CI reads of the batch head. The lease is renewed before each read.
The project lease TTL the lane asks for (PJL_TTL_S; 900 is the route's max). Renewed on every CI poll and while the setup and apply commands run.
Wall time of MIGRATION_LANE_SETUP_CMD (for example npm ci) in the apply tree. It runs only when package-lock.json changed since the last setup.
Wall time of MIGRATION_LANE_APPLY_CMD, the project's own migration ledger CLI. Its exit code alone never counts: each file must show in migrations/status with the staged checksum.

The project's migration ledger CLI, run in a main tree with only the batch's SQL files copied in (project-6: node scripts/db/apply-sql.mjs). Read by bin/migration-lane.sh from env/<project>.env. NOT settable from the control plane: it is a command a root lane runs with the production database credential.

Optional install step for the apply tree (for example npm ci --ignore-scripts). Read by bin/migration-lane.sh from env/<project>.env. NOT settable from the control plane: it is a command a root lane runs.

The production DATABASE_URL the apply command gets in its environment only (never argv, never a log). Read by bin/migration-lane.sh from env/<project>.env. NOT settable from the control plane: it is a credential.
